classification.difficultyReason: Invent a quadrilateral assembled from three equilateral triangles and verify that three congruent copies can be rearranged into a larger equilateral triangle, with neither dissection supplied.

content.prompt: I am a quadrilateral. Three copies of me will make an equilateral triangle. Three copies of an equilateral triangle will make me. What do I look like?

answer.short: An isosceles trapezium made from three congruent equilateral triangles. Its parallel sides have lengths in the ratio $2:1$.
answer.worked:
Join three congruent equilateral triangles to form an isosceles trapezium. Its shorter base equals one triangle side and its longer base equals two triangle sides.

Three congruent copies of this trapezium fit together to form an equilateral triangle, as shown.
